title: Creator Shortlisting

paragraphs: At the NYU SPS × Google Hackathon, our team is building a tool to turn a brand brief into a shortlist of relevant creators. I contributed to feature design and owned analytics metric design and interactive page logic, including LLM integration.

sections.title: System Design
paragraphs: The workflow collects campaign requirements conversationally, identifies timely topics, retrieves recent creator data, and produces ranked, budget-aware recommendations.
bullets: YouTube Data API supplies recent videos, statistics, and comments.
A weighted score combines engagement, stability, momentum, and publishing consistency with LLM-assessed audience fit, content quality, and brand safety.
Hard filters record why a creator is excluded; an estimated-cost 0/1 knapsack step compares under-, at-, and over-budget options.

sections.title: Implementation
paragraphs: I built the core interactive logic and explainable ranking workflow. Metrics distinguish observed data from AI-inferred judgments; frontend visual design was handled by a teammate.

sections.title: Evaluation & Limits
paragraphs: The prototype remains in development. An informal comparison with three friends suggested faster shortlisting, but it was not a controlled study and is not presented as a validated efficiency benchmark. Competition results were pending in the supplied record.

cardDescription: A creator-shortlisting prototype for comparing candidates and supporting human review.
note: Prototype, not a production marketing system. No award is claimed.
summary: A conversational creator-discovery prototype with explainable scoring and budget-aware shortlists.

title: E-commerce Growth & Repurchase

paragraphs: Which purchase paths convert, how does a promotion change demand, and who should receive a follow-up? This project examines those questions using 12,256,906 public Tianchi behavior records from 10,000 users. The analysis window is December 6–14, 2014.

sections.title: Data & Methodology
paragraphs: DuckDB SQL handles cleaning, user–item tables, funnel calculations, retention, and feature engineering. Features use December 6–11; purchase labels use December 12–14 to prevent future-information leakage. Logistic-regression intent scores are evaluated with out-of-fold predictions.
bullets: Compare four purchase paths at consistent user–item grain.
Track the December 6 active-user cohort for D1, D3, and D7 retention.
Use purchase history and predicted intent to form an operational segmentation matrix.

sections.title: Findings & Impact
bullets: Cart-assisted conversion reached 21.07%, versus 0.94% for direct purchase.
Within the nine-day window, 4,270 of 6,881 buyers purchased on at least two days: 62.05%.
Double-12 purchases rose 4.69× on 1.6× traffic; the top 10% intent segment converted at 84.3%, a 1.58× out-of-fold lift.

images.caption: Purchase-path conversion chart extracted from the executed source notebook.
images.alt: Original notebook chart comparing conversion rates for four purchase paths

sections.title: Business Recommendations
paragraphs: Prioritize cart recovery within 24–48 hours, align promotional messaging with observed purchase timing, and use the purchase-history × intent matrix to prioritize outreach. These are proposed actions, not measured intervention results.

sections.title: Scope & Limits
paragraphs: Repeat purchase is defined within a nine-day window. The dataset has no monetary or campaign-cost fields, so no ROI or revenue claim is made. The matrix’s value axis means purchasing history, not spend.

coverAlt: Purchase-path conversion comparison from the executed e-commerce notebook
cardDescription: Purchase-path and repurchase analysis to identify opportunities for e-commerce growth.
summary: From purchase-path funnels to retention and purchase-intent scoring on a full public e-commerce log.

title: Advertising A/B Testing & Decisions

paragraphs: A three-arm public advertising experiment compares two targeting strategies with a control. The full log contains 2,645,958 records; cleaning leaves 2,219,999. The question is which strategy warrants a staged rollout, rather than which pooled number looks largest.

overviewBlocks.caption: Screenshot from the owner’s Data_Project repository. Rollout and click-impact figures are analytical recommendations and estimates, not realized business outcomes.
overviewBlocks.alt: Original A/B Testing Decision Dashboard showing CTR comparison, confidence intervals, daily trends and rollout recommendations

sections.title: Approach & Methodology
paragraphs: Pre-specify CTR, Bonferroni-adjusted significance at 0.0167, 80% power, and a 5% planning MDE. Use dual-path two-proportion z-tests, an A/A simulation, day-stratified CMH analysis, and sensitivity checks for same-day cross-arm users.

sections.title: Findings & Impact
bullets: Control CTR nearly doubled across days, from 0.96% to 1.82%.
Strategy 1’s pooled +46.5% lift shrank to +3.6% on day 2 (p = 0.11, not significant).
Strategy 2 remained positive on both days, with +38.1% on day 2 and approximately +124% day-stratified lift.

sections.title: Business Recommendations
paragraphs: Recommend stopping Strategy 1 and staging Strategy 2 with a 10% holdout and rollback criteria. A conservative day-2 planning estimate is about 6,900 additional clicks per million impressions (95% CI 5,800–8,100). These changes were recommended, not executed.

sections.title: Scope & Limits
paragraphs: Two days of observations cannot distinguish novelty from a day-specific traffic or placement change. No revenue, cost, or downstream conversion fields are available.

coverAlt: Original Power BI A/B Testing Decision Dashboard
cardDescription: An advertising experiment analysis that combines uncertainty checks with rollout recommendations.
summary: Separating a pooled win from a stable experiment effect, with day-level analysis and rollout recommendations.

title: AI Safety Evaluation for Health Guidance

paragraphs: The UN-ICC × NYU capstone asks whether conversational AI tools can give safe, medically accurate, age-appropriate, and locally feasible guidance for women and adolescents. My responsibility is the testing workstream.

sections.title: Evaluation Design
paragraphs: The proposed matrix crosses three health scenarios, three country contexts, and two personas: 18 standardized cases, each planned for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, for 54 test runs. Scenarios cover maternal emergencies, family planning, and adolescent reproductive health. Country contexts are Kenya, Ethiopia, and India.

sections.title: Testing Protocol
paragraphs: Hold the core health question constant, vary only the comparison variable, use a fresh conversation for each tool, and capture full prompts, responses, model/version dates, case evidence, and issue notes. DHS, EDHS, NFHS, and WHO public evidence informs case design.

sections.title: Current Status
paragraphs: The supplied record is a testing proposal: pilot runs are pending, prompt wording is not locked, and country selection requires team/sponsor confirmation. The 54-response dataset is a planned deliverable, not a completed result. No model safety conclusions are claimed.

cardDescription: A proposed evaluation framework for testing AI safety and documenting evidence.
note: Proposal-stage work; no evaluation results or completed test dataset are reported.
summary: A reproducible testing proposal for women’s and adolescent health guidance in low- and middle-income contexts.

title: Medicare Payment Benchmarking

paragraphs: How much do Medicare inpatient payments vary across states, and how should providers benchmark them? Our course team analyzed CMS fiscal-year 2023 fee-for-service data released in 2025: 146,427 hospital–DRG records, 2,945 hospitals, and 534 DRGs.

sections.title: Data & Methodology
paragraphs: Standardize identifiers and coding; flag rather than remove IQR outliers; aggregate using discharge-weighted state–DRG means. Apply descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, coefficient of variation, K-Means with three clusters, Kruskal–Wallis with Dunn–Bonferroni comparisons, and chi-square tests.

sections.title: Key Findings
bullets: Average payment differed by 2.5× between the highest- and lowest-paying states ($39,922 versus $15,674).
Among 360 DRGs with sufficient data, 95.3% exceeded the 15% coefficient-of-variation threshold.
27.5% of state–DRG observations departed from the national benchmark by more than ±20%.

sections.title: Business Recommendations
paragraphs: Use state-level benchmarks, review DRG coding and clinical documentation, and target high-variation treatment categories for audit. Recommendations were proposed; implementation effects were not measured.

cardDescription: Comparing geographic variation in inpatient payments to support state-level benchmarking.
summary: Comparing geographic variation in inpatient payments and translating it into state-level benchmarking recommendations.

title: Employee Attrition & Workplace AI Risk

paragraphs: Analyze 5,000 employee records across eight departments and 25 roles to understand attrition patterns and prioritize retention conversations. The analysis dataset is not attributed to a named employer.

sections.title: Approach & Methodology
paragraphs: Audit missingness, duplicates, and tenure consistency; retain and flag 59 tenure-inconsistent records. Compare effect sizes with Cohen’s d, fit nested multivariable logistic regressions, test interactions, and evaluate out-of-fold risk scores with calibration and decile lift.

sections.title: Findings & Impact
bullets: Overall attrition was 17.9%. Burnout and engagement showed the strongest separation.
In the multivariable model, burnout odds ratio was 1.52 and promotion stagnation 1.40 per standard deviation; perceived AI risk was a smaller independent association (OR 1.19).
Cross-validated ROC-AUC was 0.775. The highest-risk 10% contained 29% of leavers, a 2.9× lift.

images.caption: Model associations and uncertainty from the executed source notebook.
images.alt: Original notebook forest plot of employee attrition odds ratios and confidence intervals

sections.title: Recommendations & Limits
paragraphs: Use risk scores to prioritize supportive retention conversations, not automatic employment decisions. Associations do not establish causality. A non-significant pay × promotion-stagnation interaction is not proof that compensation cannot help. No production retention effect is claimed.

cardDescription: Modeling employee attrition risk and examining the factors associated with turnover.
summary: An interpretable retention-risk analysis separating individual conditions, perceived AI risk, and department differences.

title: Conversational AI Agent

paragraphs: Designed and developed a multimodal agent around a dialogue → memory → knowledge retrieval → live search → response generation workflow.

sections.title: System Architecture
paragraphs: Redis provides cross-session memory; Qdrant supports document chunking, embedding, semantic retrieval, and filtering; SerpAPI adds live information. LangChain and OpenAI GPT orchestrate responses through a FastAPI application.

title: StarShow · Concert Companion

paragraphs: Designed a concert companion covering show discovery, ticket-sale reminders, concert-day planning, seat recommendations, and memory keeping.

sections.title: Product Design
paragraphs: Mapped user needs to scenarios and solutions; distinguished favorites, watchlist, and plans; documented key flows, priorities, and a three-phase roadmap. Hypotheses and metrics are defined for future validation, not reported as measured outcomes.

paragraphs: Built a high-fidelity frontend prototype in HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript with localStorage. Seat scoring reacts to preferences; a four-stage plan covers ticket preparation, pre-trip planning, show day, and the return journey.

title: EV Battery Failure Prediction

paragraphs: Predict battery failure and examine an intervention threshold using a synthetic dataset of 200,000 records and 70 fields. The source record’s narrative remains marked pending owner review.

sections.title: Approach & Methodology
paragraphs: Exclude identifier fields; compare raw telemetry with engineered composite features; use stratified 70/15/15 train, validation, and test splits. Fit imputation and encoding only on training data. Compare dummy, logistic-regression, and XGBoost baselines using PR-AUC.

sections.title: Evaluation
bullets: Raw-feature logistic regression achieved PR-AUC 0.9172; raw-feature XGBoost achieved 0.9192, a modest improvement.
Select the threshold on validation data to maximize precision while preserving at least 90% recall. At threshold 0.7127, test recall was 90.9% and precision 75.9%.
Redundancy checks showed two leading health features represent essentially the same signal.

images.caption: Precision–recall curve from the synthetic-data source notebook.
images.alt: Original executed notebook precision-recall curve for battery failure classification

sections.title: Scope & Limits
paragraphs: Synthetic data restricts generalization. The threshold is an analytical decision rule, not a production maintenance policy. Model complexity is not presented as a large performance gain; importance is not causality.

cardDescription: Battery-failure classification using synthetic data and precision–recall evaluation.
note: Narrative pending owner review. All displayed results refer to synthetic data.
summary: A leakage-aware classification workflow, with strong baselines and recall-sensitive threshold selection.

title: EV Adoption Drivers

paragraphs: Explore where electric-vehicle adoption grows fastest and which factors are associated with it in a course-provided panel: 25 countries × 16 years × three segments, 2010–2025. The 1,200 source rows aggregate to 400 country-year observations for modeling.

sections.title: Approach & Methodology
paragraphs: Validate panel grain and KPI arithmetic; discard an inconsistent supplied growth column. Analyze share and volume separately, then fit OLS to logit-transformed share with year fixed effects, country-clustered uncertainty, wild cluster bootstrap, collinearity checks, and eight robustness specifications.

sections.title: Findings & Impact
paragraphs: In this dataset, emission regulation and charging infrastructure were the only consistently robust associations in the joint model. GDP was less stable after small-sample correction; fuel-price and subsidy effects were not significant in the main joint model.
bullets: Premium adoption generally preceded mass-market adoption; commercial vehicles trailed.
High subsidies without dense charging infrastructure were associated with lower adoption in the observed market profiles.

images.caption: Regional patterns in the course-provided dataset; not an independently validated official market series.
images.alt: Original source notebook regional EV market-share trajectories from 2010 to 2025

sections.title: Scope & Limits
paragraphs: This is observational, course-provided data with unspecified original generation/source details, not verified official registration data. Regulation and charging variables are highly correlated; model associations do not identify causal policy effects.
